title: BMDE Schema
text:
library(readr)
library(dplyr)


Attaching package: 'dplyr'

    filter, lag


The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(knitr)


BMDE Schema
The BMDE 2.0 schema, as well as a number of extensions, are published on the NatureCounts site.
Pulled the BMDE 2.0, minimum, and extended information into separate CSV files in data/external, using the R script scripts/data_processing/parse_bmde_terms.R. Note that this script will not overwrite the files if they already exist in data/external. For more details there are some examples in the script’s header comments.

source("../scripts/data_processing/parse_bmde_terms.R")
parse_bmde_terms(c("BMDE2.00", "BMDE2.00-ext", "BMDE2.00-min"))

Skipping /home/jcullis/projects/darwin-birds/data/external/BMDE2.00.csv (exists; use overwrite = TRUE / --overwrite)


Skipping /home/jcullis/projects/darwin-birds/data/external/BMDE2.00-ext.csv (exists; use overwrite = TRUE / --overwrite)


Skipping /home/jcullis/projects/darwin-birds/data/external/BMDE2.00-min.csv (exists; use overwrite = TRUE / --overwrite)


Load the BMDE files as data frames.

bmde_filenames <- c(
  min = "../data/external/BMDE2.00-min.csv",
  std = "../data/external/BMDE2.00.csv",
  ext = "../data/external/BMDE2.00-ext.csv"
)

# Load the CSV files with read_csv, with all column types set to text
bmde <- map(bmde_filenames, \(f) read_csv(f, col_types = cols(.default = col_character())))

Now each data frame can be referenced as e.g. bmde$min.
Get the column counts for each extension.

map_int(bmde, nrow)

min std ext 
 37 169 265 


Next, build a data frame that combines all the terms across these extensions, and shows which extension each term is a member of.

membership <- bmde |>
  # imap - send each df and set name ("min", "std", "ext") via anonymous function
  imap(\(df, set) df |>
         select(field) |>
         mutate("in_{set}" := TRUE)) |>
  # reduce: given a list and fn that combines, merges the three df's into one, two at a time.
  reduce(full_join, by = "field") |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("in_"), function(x) coalesce(x, FALSE)))

  head(membership)

# A tibble: 6 × 4
  field                  in_min in_std in_ext
  <chr>                  <lgl>  <lgl>  <lgl> 
1 GlobalUniqueIdentifier TRUE   TRUE   TRUE  
2 CatalogNumber          TRUE   TRUE   TRUE  
3 Locality               TRUE   TRUE   TRUE  
4 TimeCollected          TRUE   TRUE   TRUE  
5 CollectorNumber        TRUE   TRUE   TRUE  
6 FieldNumber            TRUE   TRUE   TRUE  


Build a lookup df mapping terms to their descriptions.

# One description per field, preferring the extended list, then standard, then minimum
descriptions <- bmde[c("ext", "std", "min")] |>
  bind_rows() |>
  distinct(field, .keep_all = TRUE)

head(descriptions)

# A tibble: 6 × 2
  field                  description                                            
  <chr>                  <chr>                                                  
1 GlobalUniqueIdentifier "A universal resource name for the global unique ident…
2 DateLastModified       "The last time when any of the data for the record wer…
3 BasisOfRecord          "A descriptive term indicating whether the record repr…
4 InstitutionID          "An identifier for the institution having custody of t…
5 InstitutionCode        "The code (or acronym) identifying the institution adm…
6 CollectionCode         "The code (or acronym) identifying the collection with…


Join on the field column to add the descriptions and a ‘set summary’ string column using the last two dfs above.

# Use pmap_chr -  takes a list of vectors of equal length and calls the fn once per row.
# The _chr means each call must return a string, results in char vector for new column.
fields <- membership |>
  left_join(descriptions, by = "field") |>
  mutate(
    sets = pmap_chr(
      list(in_min, in_std, in_ext),
      function(m, s, e) paste(c("min", "std", "ext")[c(m, s, e)], collapse = ", ")
    )
  ) |>
  # Keep the field order from the extended list, then any fields only found elsewhere
  arrange(match(field, bmde$ext$field)) |>
  select(field, in_min, in_std, in_ext, sets, description)

head(fields)

# A tibble: 6 × 6
  field                  in_min in_std in_ext sets          description         
  <chr>                  <lgl>  <lgl>  <lgl>  <chr>         <chr>               
1 GlobalUniqueIdentifier TRUE   TRUE   TRUE   min, std, ext "A universal resour…
2 DateLastModified       FALSE  TRUE   TRUE   std, ext      "The last time when…
3 BasisOfRecord          FALSE  TRUE   TRUE   std, ext      "A descriptive term…
4 InstitutionID          FALSE  FALSE  TRUE   ext           "An identifier for …
5 InstitutionCode        FALSE  TRUE   TRUE   std, ext      "The code (or acron…
6 CollectionCode         FALSE  TRUE   TRUE   std, ext      "The code (or acron…


Summarize the number of fields that are members of each combination of sets.

summary <- fields |>
  count(sets, name = "n_fields") |>
  arrange(desc(n_fields))

summary

# A tibble: 3 × 2
  sets          n_fields
  <chr>            <int>
1 std, ext           132
2 ext                 96
3 min, std, ext       37


We see that many set combinations don’t exist, e.g. min on its own, thus we can conclude based on the combinations that do exist that the three sets of terms fit cleanly within each other.
Write the fields df to CSV.

write_csv(fields, "../data/processed/bmde_set_info.csv")

title: tdwg_dwc_terms
text:
library(readr)


TDWG Darwin Core Terms
TDWG maintains information about the standard DwC terms in a few different places:

The Darwin Core Quick Reference Guide website.
The list of terms on the TDWG GitHub repository
The list of ‘simple’ DwC terms on the TDWG GItHub repository

We will first run a script pull most of the information from the Quick Reference Guide (QRG) site (omitting the term examples text) into a local CSV, saved to ../data/external/tdwg_dwc_quick_reference_terms.csv, and also load it into a tdwg_terms dataframe. The QRG site usually lists a class / term collection name prior to listing the terms that are part of this class/collection. The script only creates new rows for terms, but adds the term’s class membership as a separate column. For more details see the comments in the script header.
Note that the script will overwrite the existing CSV by default. It may be worth checking the TDWG GitHub term_versions.csv file prior to running this script to see if new terms have been released since it was last run.

source("../scripts/data_processing/parse_tdwg_dwc_terms.R")
tdwg_terms <- parse_tdwg_dwc_terms()

A few notes about the DwC QRG page:

Two sections, as listed, aren’t technically classes. “Record-level” (8 terms) and “UseWithIRI” (119 terms) are page sections, not classes, so their terms get the section name in the class column. UseWithIRI holds the IRI versions of terms from many different classes.
Class assignment follows the page layout. For example, ecoiri:absentTaxa sits under MachineObservation on the page, so that’s the class it is assigned.
Classes with no terms don’t appear. Classes like LivingSpecimen and PreservedSpecimen have no terms of their own, so they aren’t in the CSV.

Next, pull the list of TDWG terms from the GitHub page - all terms in vertical format, as well as the set of ‘DwC simple’ terms.

Darwin Core Term Versions
The Darwin Core terms are versioned in GitHub here: https://github.com/tdwg/dwc/raw/refs/heads/master/vocabulary/term_versions.csv
Also downloaded BMDE 2.00 to data/external.
The AKN paper introducing BMDE was published in 2009, though it sounds as though the BMDE standard may have been developed and circulated online around 2005 or 2006.
The first release of DwC was 2009-10-09, though there are dates earlier than this for terms in the above term_versions.csv.
We will first load and take a look at the first rows in the term_versions.csv.


Code
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(knitr)

TERM_VERSIONS_URL <- "https://github.com/tdwg/dwc/raw/refs/heads/master/vocabulary/term_versions.csv"
BMDE_FIELDS_CSV <- "data/external/bmde_2.00_fields.csv"
DWC_RATIFIED <- as.Date("2009-10-09") # TDWG ratification of the first DwC standard
TODAY <- Sys.Date()

Function to get the terms that were in use on a given date.


Code
dwc_snapshot <- function(on_date) {
  term_versions |>
    filter(issued <= on_date) |>
    arrange(issued) |>
    group_by(term_iri) |>
    slice_tail(n = 1) |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(status != "deprecated")
}


Now we can get the terms in use in 2009 vs those in use today.


Code
dwc_2009 <- dwc_snapshot(DWC_RATIFIED)
dwc_today <- dwc_snapshot(TODAY)
